statement: Accuracy per step is set by the structure of the update. Only effects of about 0.6 pp or more are robust under the corrected noise model (~0.2 pp sd on a 3-seed mean, ~0.28 pp on an unpaired difference). These are: Muon on the conv filters (+1.3 pp, E014), lookahead (~0.9-1 pp, E008/E020), the Muon lr cliffs (0.36: E019; 0.12: E075), frequency-split orthogonalization (E030), whitening weaker than NS3 (E065) and a 1x1 final map (E050). Most other closures (E033, E036, E046, E049, E060, E066, E068, E072) and the force-keeps (E024, E026, E042, E045, E052) are single runs within ~1-2 sd. So 'the update geometry is saturated' is NOT established. The recipe may be a random walk over flat directions. The Polar Express gain (E069) is doubtful: its 13-seed mean is ~0.7534, and both the PE paper's own CIFAR runs and MUD's airbench table find no gain from stronger orthogonalization. Remaining directions should be screened offline on 10-20+ seeds in one process for TRUE-mean gain: averaging setup (H1.6.1), schedule shape (new), logit scale (new), the airbench96 residual check (new), and the width split (H1.12).

An airbench96-style network without TTA (frozen 2x2 patch-whitening, dirac init, BN-bias lr x64, lookahead, alternating flip, depth 3, widths 128/384/576, lr 9, wd 0.012, bs 1024) works as the base recipe. With SGD it clears 0.753 at 9-10 epochs in ~8-9 s on the A100-SXM4. It is now the backbone of the Muon tip.
Without TTA, the airbench96-style recipe (128/384/576, depth 3, LS 0.3) at <=10 epochs reaches mean accuracy >=0.753 on seeds 0-2, with time <=12 s on the A100-SXM4. The baseline is 59.3 s.
For the current recipe the knee lies in (8.5, 9] epochs. At 8.5 epochs (lr/lookahead schedule compressed to the shorter run) the mean is <0.753; at 9 epochs it is >=0.753.
Between 8 and 11 epochs, accuracy rises by >=0.4 pp per extra epoch and roughly linearly. So the knee at 0.753 can be found to within 0.5 epochs (about 5% of time) from a 3-4 point epoch sweep.

Muon on the 4D conv filters cuts the epochs needed on CIFAR-100 by ~2.5 (9 SGD epochs -> ~6.5-6.75 Muon epochs). The working form is flattened [out, in*k*k] orthogonalized Nesterov momentum, NS3 at Frobenius scale 1, and weight-norm projection. Nesterov SGD runs the BN biases, the whitening bias and the head, and lookahead is kept. The Muon lr has cliffs on both sides: 0.36 costs ~1 pp (E019) and 0.12 costs ~0.6 pp against E069's 13-seed mean (E075). The plateau between them (0.16-0.24, plain NS3) was measured with single runs. Whitening below NS3 is a cliff (E065 -1.51; MUD's MUD1 is ~0.7 pp below Muon5 on airbench). Whitening above NS3 is flat on the best evidence: E017 NS5 ~= NS3, MUD Muon3 ~= Muon5, the PE paper's CIFAR runs show no gain, and E069's 13-seed mean is ~0.7534. Frequency-split (E030) lost clearly. NorMuon (E066) and bs 2048 (E055) were single negative runs.

Muon (lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, Nesterov, 3 NS steps, flattened filters) on the conv filters only, with lookahead, bs 1024 and the 9-epoch schedule kept, gives >=+0.3 pp mean accuracy over the tip at 9 epochs. That is enough to reach >=0.753 in >=10% less time (<=7.3 s) at its own knee.
With 100 classes and short training, stronger label smoothing (about 0.3) regularizes better than the CIFAR-10 default of 0.2, raising accuracy at a fixed epoch count.
At a fixed recipe and epoch count, LS 0.3 gives >=0.3 pp higher mean accuracy than LS 0.2. LS 0.4 is no better than 0.3 (within 0.15 pp or worse).
Training only on the hardest examples, scored by loss under a cheap proxy model, saves enough compute per epoch to outweigh the proxy's overhead even in an approximately 10-epoch regime.

Backpropagating only the hardest 50% of each batch, ranked by loss from the main model's own forward pass (no separate proxy), reaches >=0.753 with >=10% less time than full-batch training at the matched knee.
Adding width to the later blocks buys accuracy at about the same rate as adding epochs, not clearly more cheaply. Late blocks run at small spatial size, but time still scales close to FLOPs.

Widening the last block from 576 to ~768 (or the middle block from 384 to ~448) at 9 epochs gives >=0.3 pp mean accuracy for <=5% more time per epoch. The net time at the 0.753 knee is lower than the current tip (8.09 s).

With the recipe held fixed, per-trial GPU work can still be cut by a few percent, but only by removing GPU work: launch overhead is hidden (E005, E038). Math-preserving cuts found so far: E078 fused per-epoch augment (-2.5%), E077 build-time prepare warmups (-1.3%), and E081 bundling both (-3.7%). All three failed the gate on process-level re-draws, not on their effect. They become gate-neutral only if kernel selection is made deterministic across processes (H2.5.1); otherwise every 'math-preserving' cut is a ~50% lottery at E069's true mean of ~0.7534. Earlier systems total: ~11% (E007, E010, E021, E023, E034), plus the curriculum (H2.3) and the block-1 freeze (E058 -4.7%). Smaller levers left: Gram NS (<=~1% end to end, math-changing), projection frequency (H2.4.3, math-changing), and remaining outside-step overhead (new H3 child).

torch.compile (max-autotune) with channels_last and fp16/bf16 autocast (BatchNorm in fp32) raises throughput substantially. Compilation and warmup happen in build() on synthetic data, so they are untimed.
A compiled, channels_last, half-precision training step cuts train time by >=20% against the same recipe run eagerly in fp32/TF32. Mean accuracy changes by no more than 0.2 pp.

The remaining time in a run of a few seconds is dominated by per-step overhead outside the kernels (Python/launch, per-parameter optimizer loops), so a vectorized or fused optimizer update and a fully compiled train step cut time substantially.
On top of H2.1, a fused/foreach optimizer plus a single compiled train step (forward, backward and update) reduces time by >=8%, with accuracy within 0.2 pp.

A resolution curriculum of bilinearly downsampled whole images (antialiased, inside the compiled augment) cuts FLOPs at small accuracy cost while the low-res steps fall in or near warmup. Current form: 20 px for epochs 0-1.5, 28 px for 1.5-3.5, then 32 px for 3.25 epochs. Prices: 24 px warmup -3.0%/+0.08 pp (E040); 24->20 px -3.5%/-0.18 (E047); 28 px stage -5.2%/+0.02 (E048, -0.23 in E044); 28 px to 3.5 epochs -1.5%/-0.10 (E051); 28 px to 4.0 epochs -1.6 to -2.3%/~-0.2 (E054, E074, both infeasible). 16 px collapses (E050 -1.41, 1x1 final map). Fable's CIFAR-10 SOTA independently uses 24->28->32. The 32 px tail is at its floor.

Running the first ~35% of epochs at 24 px and the rest at 32 px reaches >=0.753 with >=8% less time than training at 32 px throughout. The comparison is at the matched knee and may allow added epochs.

Fixed and per-epoch overheads outside the train step are a few percent of the score, not >10%: ~4% at a ~4.6 s run (E077 prepare first-use -1.3%; E078 per-epoch augment/permute/gather -2.5%, from 0.16 to ~0.06 s/trial). Their share grows as step time shrinks: E003 measured ~2% at 8.3 s. They can be cut bit-identically by moving warmups into build() and writing only consumed samples.

Keep the whole training set on the GPU as a uint8/half tensor, loaded in prepare, and run augmentation (flip, translate/crop, cutout) as vectorized GPU ops. This removes the bottleneck of a 4-CPU dataloader.
With data and augmentation on the GPU, prepare (load, transfer, normalize, whitening fit) takes <=1.0 s, and per-epoch time is not CPU-bound: GPU utilization stays >=90% during train.

Every compile, autotune and warmup happens in build() on synthetic inputs, covering every shape used later (full and final partial train batch, eval batch sizes). That way nothing recompiles inside the timed region, and no real data is touched in build.
After warmup in build, the first epoch's time is within 10% of later epochs, and no recompilation happens during prepare or train. Eval of any batch size B=1..1024 finishes in <5 s.

The binding constraint is the LOCAL accuracy gate (3-seed mean on fixed seeds 0-2 >= 0.753), not the official one. E069's true (13-seed) mean is ~0.7534, so any edit, including math-preserving ones, passes with probability ~50-55%: every edit changes build() state, which changes the autotuned kernels and re-draws all seeds (E077). The 3-seed mean sd is ~0.2 pp. E070-E081 all missed, including four real time cuts (E077, E078, E080, E081). Per Jordan (2304.01910), seed variance is mostly test-set sampling noise, so no recipe change can shrink it. The only ways through are: (a) a higher true mean, about >=0.7555 for >=85% pass probability (H4.5); or (b) deterministic kernel selection, so math-preserving cuts inherit the base's draw (H2.5.1). Score candidates against 13-20+ seed means, never against seeds 0-2 deltas below ~0.3 pp.

Noise on the local gate is dominated by build-perturbation nondeterminism. An unchanged commit reruns bit-identically (E003; I102 on E069). But any edit that changes build() state (warmups, graph set, allocator) shifts cudnn.benchmark/max-autotune kernel choices, and the ~220-step chaotic run turns the different rounding into a full per-seed re-draw. E077, math-identical and verified bit-identical offline, moved seeds by -0.25/+0.14/-0.84 pp. The effective sd for ANY code change is ~0.2 pp on the 3-seed mean and ~0.35-0.4 pp per seed (Jordan's sqrt(err(1-err)/n) gives the same order). E057's 0.06 pp was one draw and understates it.
Rerunning an identical (bit-identical commit) recipe gives a spread in mean accuracy of <=0.15 pp and a spread in mean time of <=3%.
Weight averaging (lookahead or EMA) raises accuracy strongly at low epoch counts on CIFAR-100: about 1 pp at 9 epochs, worth ~1-2 epochs. That is much more than on CIFAR-10 (about 11% of epochs).
Removing lookahead from the airbench96-style base costs >=0.3 pp of mean accuracy at a fixed epoch count (about 1 epoch).

With lookahead heavily weighting late iterates, the end of training matters through what it feeds the average. A non-zero tail lr supplies diverse iterates: decay-to-0 hurt (E025 -0.51 pp), a 0.15x floor was not better (E033 -0.17), and BN recalibration adds nothing (E035). The averaging setup itself (decay, sync interval, ramp exponent, EMA on top) is effectively untested. Averaging is worth ~1 pp (E008, E020), and its one tuning run (E028) matched its parent to 0.003 pp. This is the cheapest margin-recovery axis (<1% time).

On the current base (E081 code, deterministic kernels if H2.5.1 holds), after the H1.6.6 check, a stronger or denser averaging setup gives >=+0.15 pp in TRUE mean at <=1% more time. Screen offline in ONE process on >=20 seeds, and launch only a candidate whose paired gain is >=2 SE. Candidates in priority order: (t/T)^2 instead of (t/T)^3 ramp; lookahead sync every 3 steps instead of 5; a late-started EMA on top of lookahead, initialized from the current weights (hlb-CIFAR10 starts its EMA for the last ~80% with a cubic ramp).
At 9 epochs, a sharper lr anneal over the final ~15% of steps gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy with time unchanged. Candidates: a faster decay to zero in the last epoch, or a lower terminal lr.
Combining the best averaging and tail changes (N1a/N1b) lets the recipe clear 0.753 at 8.5 epochs, with time <=7.75 s on top of the E010 systems changes.

The SGD-group lrs are flat within about +-0.3 pp around head x2 / BN-bias x64. Only the clearly worse sides are established: head x0.5 (-0.41, E039) and BN x128 (-0.49, E056), each a single run of ~1.5-2 sd. Head x2 (E045 +0.18), x3 (E049 -0.03) and BN x32 (E072 -0.13 vs the lucky tip, ~+0.14 vs E069's 13-seed mean) are all within noise, so the optimum is unresolved. This still rests on the multipliers actually being applied in the compiled path (H1.6.6).

At the tip's epoch count, at least one remaining one-factor change to the SGD group beats the tip's mean accuracy by >=0.25 pp. Candidates: head lr x1.5 or x2 (lr*wd constant), or BN-bias lr multiplier 64 -> 32 or 128. Head lr x0.5 is already ruled out (E039 -0.41 pp).
The tip recipe (E010) at 8.75 epochs, with the schedule scaled to the step count, reaches mean accuracy >=0.753 in <=7.9 s. Expected accuracy is 0.751-0.755.

Non-conv or redundant work that takes a visible share of GPU time can be cut at no accuracy cost by doing less of it. Instances: the atomic pool backward (E010 -2.0%), SiLU (E021 -2.2%), a batched compiled Muon step (E023 -2.7%), freezing the whitening bias after epoch 1 (E034 -3.0%), and freezing block 1 for the last 20% (E058 -4.7%). Further freezing gives too little: block-2 first conv -0.9% (E071), eval-mode BN in frozen block 1 -0.2% (E076). The remaining Muon cost (~1.4 ms/step, ~6% of the run) is GPU kernel time (E038). Candidates are Gram NS (stable ~-29% NS FLOPs) and projection frequency. Fewer NS iterations risk E065-style under-whitening.

Replacing GELU with SiLU (or ReLU) throughout cuts mean time by >=3% versus the tip, with mean accuracy within +-0.15 pp (re-draw noise). Before launching, run a one-step finite-gradient check under compile.

Conv algorithm selection and conv shapes are not where time goes. Odd spatial sizes cost almost nothing (E032), and max-autotune/cudnn.benchmark gained ~1.1% at most (E007, within jitter). Their real cost is nondeterminism: timing-based kernel choice differs whenever build() state changes, which turns every edit into a full per-seed re-draw (E077). They also add a 77 s build and kernel choices tuned on the SXM that may not transfer to the PCIe judge.

Determinism test. Build E081 with cudnn.benchmark=False and torch.compile without max-autotune. Also check whether Inductor's Triton pointwise/reduction autotuning in torch 2.4 can change reduction order, and pin or disable any such config benchmarking. Prediction: per-seed accuracies on seeds 0-2 reproduce bit-identically across two processes whose build() warmups differ, and mean time stays within +1.5% of autotuned E081. If so, later math-preserving cuts inherit their base's gate outcome. Launch once and accept the single harness draw; no re-rolls. Refuted if any seed differs by >0.02 pp across the two processes, or time rises >2%.

Per-layer profiling will show at least one conv shape running well below the average TFLOP/s. Changing the input padding or crop so the whitening output is 32x32 or 30x30 cuts mean time by >=3%, with accuracy within +-0.15 pp.

A faithful airbench94_muon port without lookahead scores >=0.5 pp lower mean accuracy at 9 epochs than the same Muon setup with lookahead kept, i.e. Muon's update normalization does not replace averaging.

Record the extra-seed (3-12) results that already exist. E073's note cites a 13-seed paired comparison on E058, and I098 gives E069 a 13-seed mean of ~0.7534. Prediction: E058's extra-seed mean is within 0.1 pp of E069's, i.e. the ratchet inflated both tips' seeds-0-2 scores by ~0.15-0.25 pp. Refuted if E058's extra-seed mean is <=0.7510, which would leave PE a real gain.

At ~6.5 epochs, regularization tuned for longer runs (translate 2, LS 0.2) may be too strong. Cheap augmentation that adds diversity without adding difficulty may raise accuracy per epoch. One example is per-image brightness/contrast jitter, which Hiverge uses at ~7.65 epochs on CIFAR-10.

Adding per-sample GPU jitter to the Muon tip at its epoch count gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at <=1% more time. Use Hiverge's exact settings, applied in normalized input space inside the compiled augment: inputs += U(-1,1)*0.1399, then inputs *= 1+U(-1,1)*0.1308.

On the Muon base, with optimizer and averaging fixed, no reallocation of FLOPs across width, depth or resolution beats changing the epoch count by more than ~0.03 pp per 1% of time. The Muon epoch rate is ~0.08 pp per 1% of time (slope ~0.9+-0.3 pp/epoch at 6.5-7 epochs). Evidence: E029 width 0.062 pp per 1%; E037 block-1 depth worse than epochs under Muon. The test most likely to break this band is the bilinear resolution curriculum (H2.3.2 / 28->32). On SGD, low-res epochs priced at 0.058 against 0.096 pp per 1% for epochs (E013 with corrected arithmetic), which is just past the band.

Early, full-resolution capacity is the cheapest to remove. Block-1 depth costs less accuracy per 1% of time than epochs: E015 measured 0.054 vs ~0.096 pp per 1% on SGD. Removing it and spending the time on epochs is a small net win.
On the Muon tip, cutting block-1 depth from 3 to 2 and raising epochs to match the tip's time (about +0.4 epoch, time within +-1.5%) gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy over the tip.

At matched time on the Muon tip, block-3 width 640 with epochs cut to match the tip's time (~6.2 epochs if the tip is at 6.5) gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy over the 576-wide tip. A result within +-0.2 pp supports N1 (allocation indifference) instead.

Raising the batch size from 1024 to 1536 at the tip's 6.5 epochs (~319 -> ~213 steps) cuts mean time by >=4% with mean accuracy within -0.2 pp of the tip. The saving comes from fewer per-step Muon, lookahead and projection costs plus larger GEMMs. Settings: Muon lr 0.16 unchanged (normalized updates). Muon momentum 0.6, which C0128/C0143 favour at larger batch and which was flat at bs 1024 (E026). SGD-group lr x1.5 with wd unchanged (noise scale lr*N/B, C0141). Warmup fraction kept. Lookahead unchanged. Warm up the new full and partial shapes in build() with channels_last tensors (E035 lesson). Gate: in drafts/, time a bs-1536 epoch against a bs-1024 epoch first, and skip the run if the per-epoch saving is <4%. Refuted if accuracy drops >=0.25 pp with time down <5%; in that case skip bs 2048, and ghost BN at 1024-sample groups is the follow-up.
Raising the Muon group's terminal lr floor from 0.07x to 0.15-0.2x at the tip's epoch count, with nothing else changed, gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at unchanged time.

After training, recompute BN running statistics for the lookahead-averaged weights with a short timed no-grad forward over ~10-20 training batches. This gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at <=2% more time, because the averaged weights no longer match the BN buffers accumulated along the fast trajectory.

Train the whitening-layer bias only for the first ~0.5-1 epoch, then switch to a compiled graph variant without the whitening-bias gradient, so the backward skips the input-grad of block 1's first full-resolution conv. This cuts mean time by >=2% with accuracy within +-0.2 pp (airbench94_muon, Hiverge and Fable all train it only early).

Applying the Muon weight-norm projection only every 2+int(15*progress) steps (Hiverge's exact rule) instead of every step cuts mean time by >=1.5% with true-mean accuracy within +-0.15 pp. Caveat (search): Hiverge pairs intermittent projection with Muon weight decay, which the tip lacks, so weight norms may drift between projections. This change alters the math, so judge it on an offline same-process screen of >=20 seeds, not on seeds 0-2.
Capturing the batched Muon step (foreach momentum, NS3 bmm, projection) in a CUDA graph with static lr tensors cuts its time from ~1.43 to <0.6 ms/step and mean time by >=3%, with the math unchanged.

On the Muon base, a bilinear whole-image resolution curriculum (first third of epochs at 24 px, middle third at 28 px, last third at 32 px) with total epochs raised ~15% reaches >=0.753 at >=5% less time than the tip. It needs per-resolution compiled graphs and a flatten(2).max(2) global pool, checked with debug_nan.
On the Muon tip at its epoch count, lowering label smoothing from 0.2 to 0.1 gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy, because short horizons prefer weaker regularization (Hiverge uses 0.09).

On the Muon tip at its epoch count, removing translate-2 in ALL stages (including 32 px), while keeping the alternating flip, gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at equal or lower time. Untested: E052 removed translate only in the 20/28 px stages, which is a different test (see the new low-res-translate node).

Offline on extra seeds 3-10 at the same epoch count, the tip (Muon lr 0.16, momentum 0.8) and the E023 settings (lr 0.24, momentum 0.6) differ in mean accuracy by <0.15 pp. That would mean the E024/E026 keeps were re-draws, and the tip's expected margin over 0.753 is below its observed 0.16 pp.

On the tip, three numerically different but math-neutral edits and one RNG-shifting edit each move the 3-seed mean by <=0.08 pp. Example neutral edits: NS accumulation in fp32 vs bf16, reordered foreach updates, a different but equivalent lookahead blend expression. Example RNG-shifting edit: one dummy torch.randn in prepare before the permutations. This means the paired sd on the Muon base is <=~0.06 pp. The RNG-shifting edit moves the mean more than the RNG-preserving ones. Run offline in drafts/ where possible.

Some hyperparameter edits did not take effect in the timed path, through a code-path bug rather than compile caching. Dynamo guards Python floats on their exact value, so a changed constant recompiles rather than being silently ignored. Check offline in drafts/ on E069: (1) log the per-sync lookahead alpha actually applied; (2) log the effective per-step lr of each SGD sub-group (head, BN biases, whitening bias) and the Muon lr; (3) compare seed-0 final-weight hashes for E027 vs E028 and E047 vs E049. Supported if any pair is bit-identical or a logged value ignores its edit. In that case reopen the affected axes: lookahead first, then head/BN lr (E039/E045/E056/E072 would then have been wd-only changes).

How strongly Muon orthogonalizes should be scheduled over training, with weaker, less whitened updates late. E065 refuted the RMS-matched form (-1.51 pp). Search shows Hiverge's actual schedule (Frobenius 0.50->0.08 before NS3) is not RMS-matched. It shrinks the update size and comes paired with lr 0.205, intermittent projection and Muon weight decay, so E065 tested a different mechanism from Hiverge's. Either way, less whitening at matched update size hurts on this base.

On the tip at 6.5 epochs, rescale each momentum matrix before NS3 to a Frobenius norm that decays linearly from 0.50 to 0.08 over training, instead of normalizing to 1. Weight-norm projection, the lr schedule and everything else stay unchanged. This gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at unchanged time. Risk: smaller updates act like a Muon lr below 0.16, which has never been tested.

On the tip at 6.5 epochs, doubling the head lr in the SGD group, with lr*wd held constant (wd halved), gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at unchanged time. E039 showed halving it cost 0.41 pp. If x2 overshoots, x1.5 is the follow-up.

On the bs-1536 Muon base, inserting a 1.5-epoch 28 px stage between the low-res warmup stage and 32 px, at unchanged total epochs (6.75) and step-indexed schedules, cuts time by >=3% with mean accuracy within -0.25 pp. (Rewritten to match what was run. The original specified 3 epochs at 28 px and a 7.0-epoch total.)

Cutting NS from 3 to 2 iterations with Turbo-Muon AOL preconditioning saves >=0.25 ms/step and >=1.2% mean time, with accuracy within +-0.15 pp. Gate in drafts/: on the tip's real momentum matrices, launch only if the fraction of singular values >0.5 after NS2+AOL is at least NS3's. Otherwise retire.

Time is set by full-resolution compute after warmup. Warmup steps tolerate low resolution (E040, E047, E048; 18 px in E080) but not fewer steps (E053). Low-res steps after the lr peak cost ~0.2 pp per half-epoch moved from 32 to 28 px (E043, E054, E074 vs the 13-seed mean). The final map must stay >=2x2 (E050, E080). The epoch slope at the knee is uncertain by ~3x. Against E069's 13-seed mean, E070 is ~-0.36 pp for -0.25 epoch (~1.4 pp/epoch). E063's +0.07 for +0.25 epoch is a single run on another base. It must be measured directly offline (H4.5 child) before E081's savings are spent on epochs.

The 16 px collapse (E050, -1.41 pp) comes from a structural threshold: at 16 px the final map is 1x1, so global max-pool selection vanishes. The other candidate, the whitening bias being fitted at low res and then frozen, is now unlikely: training it through 3.5 epochs gave no gain (E060 -0.14).

On the E048 tip, training the whitening bias through the end of the 28 px stage (epoch 3.0) instead of epoch 1, with both graph variants warmed up in build(), raises mean accuracy by >=+0.2 pp at <=1.5% more time. If it does, the bias freeze is what limits how cheap the early phase can be. A change within +-0.1 pp refutes the confound at 20 px.

Diagnostic. On the tip, replacing the 20 px first stage with 18 px keeps a 2x2 final map (whitening 17 -> pools 8/4/2), and mean accuracy stays within -0.25 pp of the tip. A loss of >=0.6 pp would mean the 1x1-map story does not explain E050. Time saving is expected to be <1% (E050: 20->16 px saved only 0.8%, since small maps are latency-bound), so this is mainly a mechanism test.

In the low-res stages, small feature maps are latency-bound (E050 saved little time), and warmup steps tolerate low fidelity (E040, E047). So a larger batch there raises throughput and cuts steps where they matter least. It should not cost the accuracy that a flat bs increase cost (E041, -0.26 pp).

On the E048 tip, use bs 3072 in the 20 px and 28 px stages and keep bs 1536 at 32 px. Index all schedules by samples seen, keep Muon lr and momentum unchanged at the switch, and leave the SGD-group per-sample lr unchanged. Gate it in drafts/ first: skip the run if the per-epoch saving of the low-res stages is <15%. Prediction: mean time falls by >=2.5% with mean accuracy within -0.2 pp. Do not move a resolution boundary in the same run (C0235).
The final 32 px stage acts as a FixRes-style fine-tune. Post-warmup steps need near-full resolution, but 28 px may be close enough to replace part of the 3.75-epoch 32 px tail.

On the E048 tip, extend the 28 px stage from 1.5 to 2.25 epochs and shorten the 32 px stage from 3.75 to 3.0, keeping 6.75 total epochs and the step-indexed schedules. Prediction: mean time falls by >=2.5%, and accuracy stays >=0.753 and within -0.2 pp of the tip. If it loses >=0.35 pp, as E043 did, the post-warmup steps need 32 px and the tail is at its floor.

Muon lr below the tested range. On the PE tip (E069), lowering the Muon lr from 0.16 to 0.12 (0.12 was run, not the originally specified 0.11) with nothing else changed moves mean accuracy by no more than +-0.2 pp.

Late batch ramp. On the E048 tip, keep bs 1536 until ~70% of samples seen, then switch to bs 2048 for the rest of the 32 px stage. Index schedules by samples seen, keep Muon lr and momentum unchanged, and warm up all shapes in build(). Prediction: mean time falls by >=2% with accuracy within -0.2 pp. A drop of >=0.25 pp is read as over-annealing (C0209, as in E025); the follow-up is a smaller final batch.

NorMuon. On the E048 tip, add per-row second-moment normalization after NS3 (NorMuon) in the batched compiled Muon step, keeping the weight-norm projection. Prediction: >=+0.25 pp mean accuracy at <=1% more time. Untested on CNN filters.

The 100-way head is the only SGD-group parameter that has proved sensitive (E039). Its update geometry, as opposed to its lr scale, may be limiting: an SGD head update is dominated by a few frequent-gradient directions. Giving it a normalized or orthogonalized update balances the class directions.

On the E048 tip, optimize the [100, 576] head with Muon (NS3, momentum 0.8, lr chosen so the first-step update RMS matches the current SGD head's), removing it from the SGD group. Prediction: >=+0.25 pp mean accuracy at <=1% more time.

Two NS iterations with Polar Express coefficients recomputed via optimal_composition(num_iters=2, l = measured smallest singular-value ratio of the tip's momentum matrices) save >=0.2 ms/step and >=1% mean time, with accuracy within +-0.2 pp. Do not truncate the published 5-step list. Gate in drafts/: launch only if the post-NS spectrum (fraction >0.5) matches or exceeds NS3's.

FreezeOut-style: freezing block 1 (conv weights and BN biases) for the last ~20% of samples, through a compiled variant that detaches block 1's output plus a Muon variant without its group, cuts mean time by >=3% with accuracy within -0.2 pp (E058: -4.7%, -0.09 pp). An earlier freeze at 0.7 costs ~0.11 pp paired over 13 seeds on E058 (E061/E073). That is real but small, and it cannot fit the local gate's ~0.04 pp budget. Annealing before the freeze adds nothing (E067). The block-2 cascade (E062 -0.49) and mid-run thinning (E064 -0.54) are worse. The freeze point is settled at 0.8.

Offline in drafts/ on seeds 3-12, the E048 tip with the 28 px stage and the same commit without it (the E047 config) differ in mean accuracy by <=0.12 pp. That would mean the E044 (-0.23) vs E048 (+0.02) gap was re-draw noise, not an interaction with the 20 px stage or the head lr.

Augmentation strength should rise with resolution. On the E048 tip, turning off brightness/contrast jitter in the 20 px and 28 px stages, and keeping it plus translate-2 at 32 px, gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at unchanged time. Caveat: translate is applied before downsampling, so it is not stronger at low res (D018).

Each block's late learning value runs out at a different time. Block 1 is nearly done by ~0.8 of training (E058 -0.09 pp for -4.7%; 0.7 costs ~0.11 pp paired over 13 seeds). Block 2 is still learning at 0.9 (E062 -0.49 pp), even its first conv alone (E071 -0.9% time, too small). Mid-run thinning hurts (E064), and early steps cannot be removed (E053). All the refinements tested have failed: annealing before the freeze (E067), eval-mode BN (E076, no time saved) and a partial block-2 freeze (E071). The axis is exhausted at the 0.8 block-1 freeze.

Part of the cost of an earlier block-1 freeze comes from stopping abruptly while the Muon lr is still well above its floor: the last fast iterates of block 1 are noisy, and lookahead pulls the slow weights onto them. Annealing block 1's own lr to zero before the freeze (FreezeOut's per-layer cosine-to-zero) lets the freeze point move earlier at no extra accuracy cost. This is not the global decay-to-0 that hurt in E025.

On E058, linearly anneal block 1's Muon lr multiplier and its BN-bias lr from the global schedule value to 0 over samples 0.6-0.7 of training, then switch to the existing block-1-frozen graph pair at 0.7 (E061's point). All other groups keep their schedules. Prediction: mean time matches E061 (about -2.8% vs E058), and accuracy is within -0.05 pp of E058, better than E061's -0.11. Run only after the extra-seed margin check (H4.1.2).

After block 1 is frozen, its forward still computes train-mode BN batch statistics and running-stat updates that no later step needs. Running the frozen block as a pure inference block (eval-mode BN, or BN folded into the conv) removes that work. Block 2 may rely on the batch-stat noise, though, which would cost accuracy.

On E058, from the 0.8 freeze onward, run block 1 in eval mode (its running stats as of the freeze, no further updates) inside the frozen graph variant. Prediction: mean time falls by >=0.7% with accuracy within +-0.15 pp. A loss of >=0.25 pp means block 2 depends on block 1's batch-stat noise.

Late learning inside block 2 is uneven. Its first conv, which reads a frozen block 1, has less left to learn than its later convs and BN affine, so it can be frozen alone without cutting gradient to anything upstream that still trains.

On E058, for the last 10% of samples, also freeze only block 2's first conv: no wgrad, removed from its Muon shape group, with block 2's later convs and BN biases still training. Prediction: mean time falls by >=1% with accuracy within -0.1 pp of E058. A loss of >=0.25 pp, like E062's, would mean all of block 2 is still learning late.

On the curriculum+freeze base, the marginal 32 px epoch is worth far less than the ~1.14 pp/epoch measured at 6.5-7 epochs on the plain Muon base: E063 bought +0.07 pp for +0.25 epoch. If that holds, the plain total epoch count is the cheapest time lever left. The alternative readings are that E063 was a noisy single comparison, or that its moved freeze points and lookahead ramp confounded it.

E058 at 6.5 total epochs: 0.25 epoch removed from the 32 px stage, stage boundaries kept in samples, block-1 freeze kept at 0.8 of total samples, and every schedule scaled to samples seen. Prediction: mean time falls by >=3% and accuracy by <=0.1 pp. A drop of >=0.25 pp restores the steep-slope picture, and E063 was noise. Run only after the extra-seed margin check, because the gate margin is 0.07 pp.

Uniform label smoothing is flat from 0.1 to 0.3 (E004, E036), but class-structured soft targets are a different, untested change. CIFAR-100's superclasses give a strong similarity structure. Online Label Smoothing builds per-class soft targets from the model's own correct predictions, giving a richer gradient per step at negligible compute (a 100x100 scatter-add).

On the tip, replace LS 0.2 with Online Label Smoothing. A 100x100 GPU matrix S, reset in prepare(), accumulates the softmax of correctly classified training samples into their class column inside the compiled step. S is column-normalized and swapped in every half-epoch, uniform/LS for the first half-epoch. Loss = 0.5*CE(hard) + 0.5*CE(soft from S). Prediction: >=+0.25 pp mean accuracy at <=1% more time. Likely failure mode: the 300-epoch gain (+1.1 pp over LS on ResNet-56) needs a stable S, which 6.75 epochs may not give.

Stronger whitening than NS3 (3 iterations with Polar Express coefficients from optimal_composition(num_iters=3), output rescaled to NS3's Frobenius norm) gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy on the tip at <=1% more time. The seeds-0-2 result (E069 +0.24 pp) is not confirmed on extra seeds: the 13-seed mean is ~0.7534, and MUD reports no gain from stronger orthogonalization on CIFAR-10 airbench. The decisive test is the paired E069-vs-E058 comparison on seeds 3-12.

Replace the tip's batched PE-NS3 with stabilized Gram Newton-Schulz: iterate on the out x out Gram matrix in fp16 with one restart after iteration 2, using the same PE coefficients and a 1.05 safety factor. Expected NS FLOPs -29% (60n^3 vs 84n^3 at aspect ratio 9, T=3). Gate in drafts/: (a) a profile of E069 shows NS bmm is >=50% of the Muon step; (b) on real momentum matrices, the fraction of singular values >0.5 matches PE-NS3 within 1 point and the max deviation is <1e-2; (c) debug_nan passes under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs. Prediction: Muon GPU time -0.2 ms/step, mean time -0.8 to -1.2%, accuracy within +-0.15 pp of E069's 13-seed mean.

Offline in drafts/, apply 3 RNG-shift edits (1, 2 and 3 extra dummy draws from the trial generator) on both E058 and E069. Prediction: the paired per-seed sd on E069 is >=1.5x that on E058, and E069's mean over the shifts falls >=0.15 pp below 0.7561 (regression to the mean). If both bases give <=0.1 pp per seed and no mean drop, the E070-E076 losses are real effects and their refutations stand.

Turning off translate-2 in the 20/28 px stages, while keeping it at 32 px, is accuracy-neutral (within +-0.15 pp; E052 +0.04 pp). Augmentation in the low-res stages is not what limits them, so EfficientNetV2-style coupling of augmentation to resolution is not a lever at this horizon.

On the tip, lowering the BN-bias lr multiplier from x64 to x32 (lr*wd held constant) gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at unchanged time. Low prior: x128 cost 0.49 pp (E056), which suggests x64 is at or slightly above the optimum, and the airbench x64 was tuned on CIFAR-10.

Official safety is not the risk. On 13 seeds E069's mean (~0.7534) sits ~0.34 pp above the official 40-seed bar of 0.75. Per Jordan, seed spread is mostly test-set noise, so the 40-seed mean is stable. With a per-run sd of ~0.35 pp the 40-seed mean has sd ~0.06 pp. The PCIe judge will autotune different kernels, which is one more unbiased draw. Pending: restate the headroom using the EMPIRICAL per-seed sd of E069's 13 existing seeds. A recipe whose 13-seed mean stays >=0.752 is officially safe even if it misses the local gate.

Regression to the mean against the local gate. Each keep was chosen partly because seeds 0-2 drew well, so any change that re-draws those seeds loses ~0.2-0.3 pp in expectation, regardless of its true effect. This is why all seven E069 children (E070-E076) lost, including near-neutral ones (E072 -0.13, E076 -0.54). It also explains why the same freeze at 0.7 cost -0.11 pp paired over 13 seeds but -0.38 on seeds 0-2 (E073). Consequences: only changes that are neutral or better in expectation can be stacked, refutations judged against the seeds-0-2 tip by margins <0.3 pp are inconclusive, and children should be scored against 13-seed means.

Re-score E070-E076 against E069's 13-seed mean (~0.7534) instead of 0.7561. Prediction: E072 (-0.13 -> ~+0.14), E071 (~+0.17) and E076 (~-0.27) fall within +-0.3 pp of the 13-seed mean, so they are re-draw-sized. E075 (-0.62) and E070 (-0.36) stay beyond it. If this holds, E073, E074 and E076 count as inconclusive on accuracy (E076 and E074 still fail on time), and E075 and E070 remain real refutations.

Rerun E069 unchanged once (same commit, fresh process, Inductor cache intact). Prediction: per-seed accuracies match within 0.02 pp. If any seed differs by more than 0.05 pp, cudnn.benchmark/max-autotune has introduced process-level nondeterminism, which adds to every delta since E007, and E003 no longer supports H4.1.1.

statement: Muon lr upward on the PE base. On E069, raise the Muon lr from 0.16 to 0.20 with nothing else changed (0-d tensor, no recompile). PE spreads the same Frobenius norm over ~95% of singular directions instead of ~86%, so per-direction rotation is smaller and the optimum may have moved up. E075 shows 0.16 sits near a lower cliff (0.12: -0.89 pp). Prediction: >=+0.15 pp against E069's 13-seed mean, checked offline on seeds 3-12. A drop of >=0.3 pp means the plateau is narrow and 0.16 is already optimal.

Paired PE test on extra seeds. Offline on seeds 3-12, using existing runs where available, E069 (PE coefficients) minus E058 (NS3 coefficients) has a paired mean delta of >=+0.1 pp. If it is <0.1 pp, the E069 gain on seeds 0-2 was a re-draw: H1.2.7 is refuted, and the plain coefficients are kept as the cheaper-to-reason-about base.

Under Muon, the block-1/block-2 width split (128/384, inherited from SGD airbench) is not optimal. Muon uses capacity more efficiently than SGD (E037: block-1 depth is worth ~2x under Muon). Shifting width between the two blocks at matched FLOPs may raise accuracy at unchanged time. Only block-3 width and block-1 depth have been varied so far.

On E069, change block widths 128/384 -> 160/352 (multiples of 32) at matched step FLOPs (within +-1.5% time), keeping block 3 at 576 and the Muon shape groups batched. Prediction: >=+0.15 pp against E069's 13-seed mean, checked on seeds 3-12. A result within +-0.15 pp means the width split is flat. Warm up the new shapes in build() with channels_last and run debug_nan.

Gate escape through true-mean margin. A recipe whose true (13-20+ seed) mean is >=~0.7555 passes the 3-seed gate with probability >=85% (sd ~0.2 pp). Reaching it lets the parked math-preserving cuts (E078, E077, E081) be stacked. The cheapest route is to spend part of E081's -3.7% on epochs or the averaging setup, and rank all candidates by offline true-mean gain per % time, not by seeds-0-2 deltas.

Offline in one process on seeds 3-22, compare E081 at 6.75 epochs with E081 at 7.0 epochs (extra 0.25 epoch in the 32 px stage, freeze kept at 0.8 of samples, all schedules sample-indexed). Prediction: +0.25 epoch raises the true mean by >=+0.2 pp (paired, >=2 SE), at time <= E069's 4.68 s (expected ~4.65 s: E081 4.51 s + ~3.5%). If the gain is <0.1 pp, the knee is flat above 6.75 and epochs cannot buy margin.

Conditional on N1a. E081 at 7.0 epochs (built deterministically if H2.5.1 holds) launched once on seeds 0-2 clears 0.753 at time < 4.678 s (E069), giving the first new feasible tip since E069. Its 20-seed offline mean will be >=0.7550.

Pairing on seed buys little for any math-changing edit. From existing offline data (E079 and E080 on seeds 3-12 vs E069), the paired per-seed sd of the delta will be >=0.25 pp, close to the unpaired ~0.35-0.4 pp, because chaotic training re-draws per-example test errors regardless of shared data order. Consequence: a 10-seed offline delta has SE ~0.1 pp, so the E079/E080 gates set at 0.05 pp could not resolve their own thresholds. Gates must be >=2 SE, or use 20-40 seeds with both arms in one process. Refuted if the paired sd is <=0.12 pp.

The logit scale (temperature) inherited from airbench96 (logits x 1/9) was tuned for 10 classes. With 100 classes it sets the softmax sharpness, the gradient sent back to the features, and the effective head lr (head x2 helped, x3 ~= x2). It may be mis-set for this task.
